h1: U Style Hotel — a modern hotel across from Rajabhat, next to 7-11 in central Sakon Nakhon
intro: If you're coming to Sakon Nakhon to sort out paperwork, drop off your kids at university, or just want a well-located stay on the main road for a few hundred baht, U Style Hotel is a name that comes up often in reviews · It's a modern-style hotel on Nittayo Road in Tha Choeng Chum subdistrict, across from Gate 1 of Sakon Nakhon Rajabhat University and right next to a 7-Eleven · What a lot of people like is that the rooms are fairly spacious and clean, plus the covered indoor parking that's hard to find for a hotel in the city center · Prices start at around ฿550/night and it's only about 4 kilometers from Sakon Nakhon Airport — good value for anyone who cares more about location and convenience than luxury

body.html: Who U Style Hotel is right for — to put it as simply as possible, U Style Hotel is a city hotel for people coming to Sakon Nakhon who want "a well-located place on the main road, with spacious clean rooms and easy parking, for a few hundred baht" rather than a luxury resort with a spa and premium service · The hotel is a modern-style building on Nittayo Road, Tha Choeng Chum subdistrict, Mueang Sakon Nakhon district, across from Gate 1 of Sakon Nakhon Rajabhat University and right next to a 7-Eleven — an easy-to-find, very convenient spot for anyone who doesn't know their way around town · It has been open since around 2011 and renovated since, so it's not a brand-new building, but it has been reasonably well kept · From real reviews across several platforms including Trip.com, Agoda, Booking.com, Traveloka and TripAdvisor, the picture is fairly consistent: the people it suits are travelers in town on business or for government work, parents visiting or dropping off kids studying at Rajabhat, couples on a short trip, and drivers passing through who want to stop for a night before moving on · Because it sits right on Nittayo Road, a main route in and out of town, plus the covered parking underneath, people who drive themselves feel more at ease than at hotels where you park out in the sun along the road · You could say it plays the "convenient and good value" card well for its price range, without trying to sell luxury — and if you set your expectations right from the start that it's a three-star hotel in the city center, you're far less likely to be disappointed

Location and getting around — this is U Style Hotel's number-one selling point, no question · The hotel sits on Nittayo Road, a main road through Sakon Nakhon, across from Gate 1 of Sakon Nakhon Rajabhat University and right next to a 7-Eleven, so you can grab food and supplies any time without going far · Within easy reach there are restaurants, coffee shops and the university-area food courts to choose from, with the friendly prices you'd expect in a student town · One thing people mention is that it's only about 4 kilometers, or roughly a 10 min drive, from Sakon Nakhon Airport (SNO), so people flying in reach the hotel quickly without a long ride, which also suits anyone with an early flight home · As for the city's landmarks, Wat Phra That Choeng Chum, the temple at the heart of the town, and Nong Han, the big freshwater lake of the Northeast, are about 3–5 kilometers away — just a few minutes by car · The evening market and walking street in the city center are around 3 kilometers away, easy to drive or grab a ride to for dinner · A big advantage is the parking: many reviews agree that there's covered indoor parking under the building, which keeps your car out of the sun and makes parking easy — something a lot of city-center hotels don't have · One small thing to note: because it's right on Nittayo Road, a big road, and in a lively university area, rooms facing the street may pick up some traffic noise or outside sound at times, so if you're a light sleeper you should ask for an interior room when you book

"Great location, right across from Rajabhat and next to a 7-11, so easy to grab things. The room was bigger than I expected and nicely clean, and parking under the building meant the car didn't sit in the sun. A few hundred baht a night is good value for coming to take care of business in town."

Room types and decor — U Style Hotel has several room types to choose from depending on group size and budget · On the booking platforms there's the Standard Room, the entry-level room with a queen or king bed for couples and solo travelers, the Standard Twin with two single beds for friends or colleagues traveling together, stepping up to Superior and Deluxe rooms that are larger and better appointed, and bigger rooms like the Suite and family rooms for those who need more space · Beds come in both 3.5-foot and 5-foot sizes depending on the room type · The decor is a simple modern style in easy-on-the-eye tones, leaning on cleanliness and function rather than flashy design · What many reviews agree on is that the rooms are fairly spacious, the beds are comfortable, the mattresses are good quality, and the rooms are clean, which is what makes people feel they're getting value for a few hundred baht · The in-room kit covers the basics: a flat-screen TV around 32 inches, air conditioning, a water heater, a fridge or minibar, and bathroom amenities · To be fair, it's worth being honest that the building has been open for a while, so some fittings in some rooms are starting to show their age, and some reviews note that a few bathrooms are fairly cramped or don't have a clear wet–dry divider · There are also some voices saying the actual rooms differ from the website photos in places — something anyone expecting the just-opened, brand-new feel should know going in · If a spacious room with newer fittings matters to you, go for a Superior level or above and ask about it when you book

Facilities, pool and common areas — let's be straight: the information about U Style Hotel's facilities isn't fully consistent across sources · The hotel's website and some platforms say there's a small swimming pool and a fitness room, while some listings on TripAdvisor and Trip.com at certain points say there's no pool — so if you're coming mainly to use a pool or gym, it's best to confirm directly with the hotel before booking to be sure, and you shouldn't count on it being available · What does exist and gets consistent praise is the covered indoor parking that keeps your car out of the sun, the in-house restaurant and cafe, a 24-hour front desk, luggage storage, laundry service and airport transfers · As for Wi-Fi, it's free and fine for basic use, though some reviews say the signal is only strong in certain spots · For picking up essentials, the location helps a lot because there's a 7-Eleven right next door, so if you're hungry late or forget something you can just walk over · The bottom line on facilities: this place covers the basics and does them well for the price, especially the parking and the location, but it's not for someone who wants to spend the whole day in the hotel with a pool and spa — and if a pool really matters to you, check carefully first or look at a hotel in town that can confirm a pool more clearly

Food and breakfast — the hotel has an in-house restaurant and cafe, and offers a buffet breakfast · Some platforms list breakfast at around 350 baht per person if it isn't included in the room rate, while some promotions bundle breakfast in, so check the terms for each room and platform carefully when you book, since both included and not-included options exist · One thing to tell you honestly is that several reviews say breakfast runs out fast on some days, especially when it's busy, so if you go down late there may not be much left — it's worth going down a bit early · The menu is basic breakfast fare, not as varied as a big hotel's · But the upside of the location is that if you don't feel like eating at the hotel, you can easily walk out to a breakfast spot or coffee shop in the university area, because they're everywhere and prices are friendly · Many people grab food from the 7-Eleven next door or eat out instead, which is part of the charm of staying in a student area where food is cheap and easy to find · Overall, food isn't a reason to come here to eat at the hotel — it's an optional extra you can take or leave, and the location makes up for it nicely

Service — service is where the real reviews split into two camps, which is worth telling honestly for fairness · On the praise side, people say many of the staff are friendly and cheerful, helpful with the basics, and the 24-hour front desk means you can check in late or ask questions at night · Some reviews praise the help when you're in town on business, the restaurant recommendations, and the parking arrangements · But on the critical side, some reviews say plainly that service is inconsistent and depends on the time and the person you get — sometimes the reception feels indifferent, or communication with foreigners isn't very smooth, and a few older voices have mentioned billing or checkout steps that left them uneasy · Overall, then, the service lands at "good enough for the standard of a budget city hotel," not the main strength to expect luxury-hotel care from · If warm service matters a lot to you, you may have to make peace with this; but if you see a hotel at this price as just needing to deliver a clean room and a smooth check-in, it passes for the money

Voices from real reviews (praise and gripes) — pulling from Trip.com, Agoda, Booking.com, Traveloka, TripAdvisor and Thai review threads, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: the location right on the main road across from Rajabhat and next to a 7-Eleven is the most repeated point, along with rooms bigger than expected, clean rooms and bathrooms, comfortable beds and good-quality mattresses, convenient covered indoor parking, easy access near the airport, and good value starting at a few hundred baht · On the watch-out side: the most-mentioned thing to know first is that the soundproofing between rooms isn't great — at times you can hear the room next door or outside noise in rooms facing the street · Next is breakfast running out fast on some days and a not-very-varied menu, some fittings in some rooms starting to age, a few bathrooms being fairly cramped or with an unclear wet–dry divider, inconsistent water pressure and hot-water temperature in some rooms, and the actual rooms differing from the website photos in places · There are also some older voices about inconsistent service · Most of these gripes are things you can manage with a little preparation and the right expectations — like asking for an interior room and going down for breakfast early — rather than big problems that keep people from coming back · On the booking platforms the overall score is in good shape, around the low 8s out of ten, which reflects that most people are still happy with the value and location

"Spacious room, nice and clean, and the location is so easy to get around. The one gripe is the soundproofing between rooms isn't great — I could hear the room next door a bit — plus breakfast runs out fast if you go down late. Next time I'll ask for an interior room and go down for breakfast earlier."

Price and value comparison — U Style Hotel's starting price is around ฿550/night at the regular rate (some promotions drop to around ฿499) · Superior and Deluxe rooms run roughly ฿700–900, and a Suite or family room goes higher depending on size and timing · Compared with other hotels in Sakon Nakhon — like The Majestic Sakon Nakhon starting around ฿1,200, Metha Palace around ฿900 or @Sakon Hotel around ฿700 — you can see U Style Hotel is in one of the most budget-friendly groups of city hotels, while still offering spacious rooms and a location right on the main road across from the university · What makes it good value is that you pay a few hundred baht but get a room many reviews confirm is spacious and clean, plus the covered indoor parking and the closeness to the airport that saves both time and travel costs · Measured by value per baht for a trip in town on business or a short stay, this place does well · But if you're serious about soundproofing, want a varied breakfast that doesn't run out, or want a confirmed swimming pool, bumping the budget up another couple hundred baht for a higher-tier hotel in town is a reasonable choice — it depends on what you weigh most

Things to know before booking — a few things help make the stay smoother · One, the soundproofing between rooms isn't great, so if you're a light sleeper or sensitive to noise, ask for an interior room that doesn't face Nittayo Road when you book or check in, and bring earplugs just in case · Two, breakfast runs out fast on some days, so if you book with breakfast included, go down a bit early — or if you're not fussed, walk out to a spot in the university area or grab food from the 7-Eleven next door · Three, the pool and fitness room info varies by source, so if you intend to use them, call to confirm directly with the hotel before booking · Four, if a spacious room with newer fittings matters to you, go for a Superior level or above and ask when you book, since the building has been open for a while · Five, if you drive yourself, the covered indoor parking is an advantage that keeps your car out of the sun · Six, during university graduation ceremonies or big events, hotels around Rajabhat can fill up fast and prices climb, so book ahead and compare prices across several platforms — Agoda, Booking and Trip.com — before deciding

The verdict — from all the real reviews, U Style Hotel is the best fit for people coming to Sakon Nakhon who want a spacious clean room, a location right on the main road across from Rajabhat and next to a 7-Eleven, covered indoor parking, and good value for a few hundred baht · Being close to the airport, easy to find, and having convenient parking makes it a good match for a trip in town on business or government work, visiting kids studying at Rajabhat, or stopping for a night while driving around the Northeast · But if you're serious about soundproofing between rooms, want a varied breakfast that doesn't run out, want brand-new in-room fittings, or expect a confirmed swimming pool with premium service, this may not be the answer, and it's worth considering a higher-tier hotel in town instead · But for a city trip where you want the best location on a limited budget, plus the convenience of driving and getting around — U Style Hotel is a good-value, well-rounded choice for a stay in Sakon Nakhon

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — U Style Hotel Sakon Nakhon

faq.q: Where in Sakon Nakhon is U Style Hotel, and what can you walk to?
faq.a: It's at 65 Nittayo Road, Tha Choeng Chum, Mueang Sakon Nakhon · across from Gate 1 of Sakon Nakhon Rajabhat University and right next to a 7-Eleven · around it are restaurants and the university-area food court · Phra That Choeng Chum and Nong Han are about a 3–5 minute drive · Sakon Nakhon Airport is about 10 minutes (around 4 km away)

faq.q: What's the starting price at U Style Hotel, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Standard rooms start at around ฿550/night (some promotions drop to around ฿499) · there's a Standard Twin around ฿650, Superior/Deluxe around ฿800 and Suite/Family going higher · prices depend on timing and platform, so compare a few sites before booking

faq.q: Does U Style Hotel have parking and breakfast?
faq.a: There's free covered indoor parking, a point many reviews praise · there's a buffet breakfast (both included in the room rate and as an add-on for around 350 baht, depending on the promotion) · good to know: breakfast runs out fast on some days, so it's worth going down early

faq.q: Does U Style Hotel have a swimming pool?
faq.a: The information varies by source — the hotel's website and some platforms list a small swimming pool and a fitness room, while some listings say there isn't one · if you intend to use the pool, it's best to call to confirm directly with the hotel before booking to be sure

faq.q: Who is U Style Hotel right for?
faq.a: It's right for travelers on business or government work, parents visiting kids studying at Rajabhat, and drivers passing through who want to stop overnight in town · it leans on a good location on the main road, spacious clean rooms, parking under the building and good value, rather than luxury facilities

faq.q: What's the noise like at U Style Hotel, and which room should you ask for?
faq.a: Many reviews agree that the soundproofing between rooms isn't great, and rooms facing Nittayo Road pick up some traffic noise · if you're a light sleeper, it's best to ask for an interior room that doesn't face the street when you book or check in, and bring earplugs just in case
